PullRequest.Title: chat: pick cloud sandbox repository fixes
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

The cloud sandbox draft's **Select repository...** button round-tripped through the Copilot Chat extension (embarassing):

renderer `workbench.action.chat.cloudSandbox.selectRepository` → extension `github.copilot.chat.cloudSessions.openRepository` → renderer `_chat.pickRepository` → extension `github.copilot.chat.cloudSessions.searchRepositories` (Octokit) per keystroke.

That contradicted `CloudSandboxApiService`'s stated goal of working in VS Code Web without an extension host, broke whenever the extension was not yet activated, and surfaced a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'placeholder')` because `undefined` arguments become `null` across the extension-host RPC.

This PR removes the extension dependency from the cloud sandbox contribution entirely.

## Changes

- **New `CloudSandboxRepositoryPicker`** (`remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxRepositoryPicker.ts`): drives the existing shared `RepositoryPicker` quick pick with the platform GitHub client from `IWorkbenchGitHubService.acquireDefaultAccountClient`:
  - empty query → `client.query.listRepositories` (`owner,collaborator,organization_member`, sorted by `updated`)
  - typed query → `client.query.searchRepositories` with `<term> in:name fork:true user:<login> org:<…>`; pasted GitHub URLs normalize to `owner/repo`
  - the viewer/org scope needs `/user` + `/user/orgs`, fetched lazily (only once a non-empty query is typed) and cached per pick
  - requests go through the platform transport, so they get shared rate-limit coordination, ETags, priority lanes and telemetry
- **`EditorCloudSandboxSessionContribution`**: drops `OPEN_REPOSITORY_COMMAND_ID` and `ICommandService`; `_selectRepository` calls a `protected _pickRepository()` that lazily creates the picker.
- **`_chat.pickRepository`**: normalizes `null` → `undefined` for its remaining extension caller.
- Repository option group description reads "Select repository...".

## Testing

- New `cloudSandboxRepositoryPicker.test.ts` asserts the request sequence (list → user → orgs → scoped search) and that an auth failure rejects without opening a picker.
- `editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts` swaps the fake extension command for the `_pickRepository` seam.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` on the picker, contribution and `RepositoryPicker` suites: 112 passing. ESLint clean.
- Manual: open a Cloud session draft in a window without a GitHub remote, click **Select repository...**, type part of a repo name and pick one → the draft's repository option updates; no notification error.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The cache ownership and REST call path are explicit, and the previous five-minute token-keyed cache is present in the replaced extension implementation. The only magnitude uncertainty is how often users reopen and search the picker; the two added critical-path requests per reopen are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Two GitHub REST requests (`GET /user` and `GET /user/orgs`) and their response parsing per reopened picker
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The extra work grows as two wire requests for every picker invocation in which the user types a non-empty query, even when invocations occur seconds apart; queries within one invocation share the promise.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased interactive search latency and repeated GitHub API/network traffic
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The extension-backed `BaseOctoKitService` cached the computed `user:<login> org:<org>...` scope by token for five minutes, so reopening the picker and searching during that window issued only the repository search request.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The replacement declares `scope` inside `pick()`, so dismissing or completing the picker discards it. The first typed query after every reopen calls `_resolveSearchScope`, which waits for `/user` and `/user/orgs` before it can issue the repository search.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `let scope: Promise<string> | undefined;` is local to `pick()`, replacing the prior service-level `_cachedUserReposScope` with five-minute lifetime; therefore every new call to `pick()` starts with an empty scope cache.
Findings.Title: Keep the repository scope cache across picker invocations
Findings.Impact: If a user cancels or completes the repository picker and reopens it to try another search, the first result is now delayed by two additional GitHub REST round trips. ETags can reduce response bytes but still require both requests and responses on the critical path.
Findings.Evidence: Line 53 creates the scope promise with per-`pick()` lifetime, line 54 populates it through `_resolveSearchScope`, and lines 91-94 perform the two parallel REST calls. The replaced implementation in `BaseOctoKitService._getUserReposSearchScope` retained the same qualifiers by token for a five-minute TTL. The new test covers only one picker invocation and confirms the sequence list -> `/user` + `/user/orgs` -> search, so it does not preserve the previous warm-reopen behavior.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain the resolved scope across picker invocations, keyed to the acquired client/account with a bounded TTL, and invalidate it when the default client/credential changes. Keep the per-pick promise coalescing and cancellation semantics for in-flight resolution.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The old contribution entered an extension-backed picker whose repository callback ignored `RepositoryPicker`'s request cancellation token; after each 300 ms pause, a new extension-host command and GitHub request could start while superseded searches continued.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Typing successive repository terms could leave stale GitHub searches running concurrently, consuming API/network capacity and delaying the latest interactive result.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new callback creates a request AbortController, aborts it when the shared picker cancels a superseded request, and passes the combined signal through `_searchRepositories` to the GitHub transport, which removes/cancels requests with no remaining waiter.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 300 called `github.copilot.chat.cloudSessions.openRepository`; that extension invoked `_chat.pickRepository`, whose command callback accepted only `query` and executed the extension search command without forwarding the request token. Added lines 58-61 now connect `requestToken.onCancellationRequested` to an AbortController and pass its signal into all repository REST/query calls. The shared picker clears the prior request token on every value change and before each update.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the cloud sandbox repository picker and load recent repositories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The select command must acquire the default GitHub client, create/show the quick pick, and complete the initial repository list before recent items are usable. On a cold client, credential identity resolution may also complete first; on a warm client it is reused.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve authentication sessions/default repository-scoped GitHub grant
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per picker opening to acquire the client, with additional credential lookups inside query operations; the credential identity itself is coalesced/cached by the client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The cloud contribution first crossed to the Copilot extension, which resolved a permissive session there; the new path removes that extension-host round trip but uses the workbench authentication service directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Client acquisition must finish before the picker is shown and queried.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List `/user/repos` with owner/collaborator/organization_member affiliation and 100-item page
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request for the initial empty query unless canceled by typing or dismissal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The extension implementation issued the equivalent one `user/repos?per_page=100&sort=updated&affiliation=...` request for the initial empty query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Recent repository items remain busy until the list completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One picker invocation and one page capped at 100 repositories; item sorting is O(100 log 100), not unbounded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active picker is retained; opening another disposes the previous one. The initial list is one request, governed by the shared GitHub request queue (global maximum 4, host maximum 2).
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The client is shared by the workbench service. A cold credential can require identity resolution; warm credentials are retained by the client. REST responses use ETags, but warm reads still perform conditional network revalidation rather than becoming zero-wire cache hits.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the command path, query call, page cap, cancellation ownership, and request queue limits are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication-service and network duration vary by host, account state, and connection; request counts and critical-path placement are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression for the initial list: it replaces extension-host IPC with an equivalent single GitHub list request and adds bounded cancellation/queueing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type a non-empty repository search during one picker invocation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the shared 300 ms debounce, the first non-empty search waits for viewer and organization scope, then issues the repository search; later searches in the same invocation reuse the scope promise and wait only for their search request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch viewer login and first 100 organizations in parallel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two requests on the first non-empty query in a picker invocation; zero for subsequent queries in that same invocation after successful resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old extension implementation performed the same two calls on a cold scope cache, but retained the resulting scope by token for five minutes across picker invocations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both responses must complete before the first repository search can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search `/search/repositories` with term, viewer/org qualifiers, sort, and 100-item page
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for each query that survives the 300 ms debounce; superseded in-flight requests are aborted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old extension issued an equivalent GitHub search for each debounced query, but the renderer-to-extension callback could not propagate cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The matching item list remains busy until the latest search completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One effective query per 300 ms pause, one result page capped at 100 repositories, and up to 100 organization qualifiers. Superseded requests are canceled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two first-use scope requests run in parallel and are bounded by the transport host concurrency of 2; the search runs after both. Only the latest debounced repository query remains attached because value changes cancel the prior request token.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Scope is promise-coalesced only within the current picker. `/user`, `/user/orgs`, and search responses use ETags in the transport; repeated identical URLs revalidate over the network. Distinct query URLs occupy bounded LRU entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: debounce, cancellation signal propagation, promise reuse, REST cardinality, and transport concurrency were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact search RTT and typing pause patterns vary, but the first-use 2+1 request chain and later one-request chain are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Within one invocation, request coalescing and cancellation are bounded and improve on the old path; no additional finding beyond the cross-invocation cache issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismiss or complete the picker, reopen it, and type another search within five minutes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every reopened pick creates a fresh local scope promise. The first typed query therefore blocks on `/user` and `/user/orgs` before the repository search, even if the same account's scope was resolved moments earlier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-fetch viewer and organizations for a scope already resolved by a prior picker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two additional requests per reopen with a typed query; for N reopened searches, 2N scope requests rather than two total during the prior five-minute TTL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: `BaseOctoKitService._cachedUserReposScope` cached by token for five minutes, making warm reopened searches issue only the search request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both requests delay each reopened picker’s first typed result before the actual search can start.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Each reopen followed by a non-empty query adds exactly two scope REST calls; cost grows linearly with picker reopen count, not repository result count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two scope requests run concurrently with each other but the search is serialized behind both. Separate picker invocations are serialized by `_currentPick`, so the issue is repeated work rather than an unbounded concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new cache lifetime ends with each `pick()` call. Transport ETags reduce warm response bytes but still require two wire round trips. Previously, the token-keyed scope remained warm for five minutes across picker invocations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the cache variable is lexically scoped to `pick()`, cleanup disposes each pick, the two REST calls are explicit, and the prior five-minute cache is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users commonly may select only once, so prevalence and aggregate traffic are uncertain; the deterministic two-request latency penalty on every warm reopen supports low severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity cache-lifecycle regression; submitted as a finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continue typing or dismiss while a repository search is in flight
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A new value immediately clears the current request token; dismissal disposes the pick. The request-specific AbortController propagates this cancellation through the query/transport path so stale work is not required for the latest result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer/extension command round trips for opening and each repository query
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one opening round trip plus one search command round trip per debounced query; removed from the changed cloud sandbox path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the base behavior removed by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously added serialization latency and prevented the renderer request token from reaching the extension’s network request; now absent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Abort superseded GitHub list/search/scope requests through a combined AbortSignal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the latest debounced query remains active for this picker, aside from bounded scope subrequests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old `_chat.pickRepository` command callback ignored its request token when invoking the extension search command, so superseded GitHub requests could continue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Stale searches no longer consume network/queue capacity needed by the latest result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Potentially one request per query surviving the debounce, but superseded requests detach/cancel instead of accumulating with the number of pauses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The shared picker has one current request token, and the transport has bounded global/host/caller queues. Scope performs at most two parallel requests; stale operations with no waiter are aborted.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful scope resolution is reused for the rest of the current pick. A canceled scope resolution clears its promise so a later query retries; this avoids retaining a rejected promise.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the request-token clearing, listener, AbortController, transport cancellation, and old command callback were all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Overlap depended on users pausing at least 300 ms between edits and on request latency, but the old inability and new ability to cancel are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a concrete performance regression fix, recorded with the introducing commit; it is not a review finding against this PR.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all six changed files and the transitive picker, extension search, GitHub credential/query, transport, and request-queue paths. Submitted one low-severity cache-lifecycle finding for losing the five-minute cross-invocation scope cache, and recorded the PR's cancellation propagation as a fix for stale concurrent searches.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
